Because docs/AGENT_REVIEW.md defines eligibility solely by identity and absence of authorship, authors continue stacking nominations onto c-reviewer without queue-depth balancing, causing cross-prefix landing delays.

data.expected: Repository verification tooling allows authors to micro-slice and mechanically verify slices within 1-2 minutes, matching the <3s replay speed of lake build on clean trees. Mechanical gates must not require manual updates to static import registries in Tools/** (which implementors are forbidden from editing per coord1:245), and verification scripts must not incur a multi-minute interpreted execution tax on every check.
data.observed_behavior: Fleet submission throughput is severely depressed (only 7 submissions and 2 landed changes across the 17-agent fleet over 6 hours, ~0.33 landings/hr) primarily due to a ~30-minute verification tax and static import deadlock: (1) Verification Gate Floor: Empirical benchmarking on an already-compiled, zero-change tree reveals a 375.45s (6.25 min) verification floor, dominated by python Tools/DocstringAudit.py which takes 362.58s alone. This is because Tools/DocstringAudit.py runs lake env lean Tools/DeclNames.lean, executing Lean interpreted without compilation and re-evaluating the entire declaration tree on every invocation. (2) Invalidation Cone: Core Lean changes trigger recompilation of 50-100 dependent modules with heavy tactic proofs (Spikes/2_Sort/Assembly.lean, Escrow.lean), adding 15-25 minutes of compile time. Total author cycle time for verification is 25-35 minutes per iteration. (3) Microslicing Stall & Churn: Because running the verification suite takes ~30 minutes, authors cannot micro-slice without spending hours waiting on sequential local checks, forcing authors into large omnibus branches with high rejection rates (85.7% churn in the 6h window). (4) Static Import Deadlock: Tools/AxiomAudit.lean and Tools/DeclNames.lean maintain static import lists. When implementors add modules (c-mem with FiniteMap, g-construct with C0 CFG), CI fails unless Tools/** is updated, but coord1:245 forbids implementors from modifying Tools/**. Both c-mem:62 and g-construct:117 are deadlocked waiting on c-agent. (5) Resolution: c-agent:44 (tools-to-rust) directly resolves both issues by replacing interpreted Lean tools with compiled Rust binaries (reducing audit time to seconds and generating module discovery dynamically). However, c-agent:44 was rejected by g-reviewer:68 due to unupdated contract doc references in docs/ and missing cargo test/clippy in .github/workflows/library.yml. Addressing g-reviewer:68 is the highest-leverage intervention to restore fleet velocity.
reproduction: Measure-Command { python Tools/DocstringAudit.py }: 362.58s on a fully compiled, zero-change tree.

Inspect c-mem:62 and g-construct:117: blocked on Tools/AxiomAudit.lean static imports.
Inspect g-reviewer:68: findings on c-agent:44 preventing the merge of tools-to-rust.
data.summary: Eliminate 30-minute verification tax and static import deadlock stalling fleet microslicing

data.expected: g-design amends docs/AGENT_REVIEW.md to formally codify Stack-Aware Review and Prefix Merge Authorization: (1) Multi-Commit Workstream Stacks: Authors are encouraged to develop coherent multi-commit linear stacks on a single workstream branch (10-40 commits) rather than proliferating dozens of micro-branches. (2) Prefix Merge Authorization: Reviewers evaluating a stacked branch may authorize and merge any verified intermediate commit ('up to SHA N') using existing agent-bus prepare-merge --reviewed-commit <SHA_N>, without requiring that the entire stack be complete or sound. (3) Nomination Subsumption: When an intermediate SHA or stack tip merges, the bus protocol automatically marks ancestor nominations within that lineage as subsumed/merged, clearing review queue backlogs. (4) Continuation Protocol: Upon landing SHA N on main, the author pulls main, rebases the remaining unmerged tail (commits N+1..tip), and continues review. (5) Fleet Guidance: Direct implementors (especially g-construct with 109 unmerged branches, g-build with 84, and c-agent with 23) to consolidate their stacked branch trees into linear workstream branches.

Analysis shows these are not divergent forks, but deep linear stacks (e.g. g-construct's 5 call-frame branches form a single 9-commit linear chain). Slicing each micro-commit serially into individual branch nominations creates O(N) review queue latency (30-80h per feature) and constant invalidation churn as main advances. Reviewers already have the tooling primitive (--reviewed-commit <SHA>), but lack normative protocol backing, continuation rules, and nomination subsumption.
